steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer, I've brought along everyone who agreed to use the bones to retreat.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Most of them wouldn't be able to withstand the long journey—the old, the young, and more injured Sarkaz than you can count.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: W said, and I quote, 'Let them die if they want,' but the other members of her squad carried them here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Somehow, she still has quite a few living subordinates—enough to maintain order within the Lifebone and watch over Ulšulah in captivity.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So at least you won't have to worry about having no one to take the wheel if you accidentally die on the road.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Got it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What are you waiting for?
The Lifebone casts a shadow over the ruins of the battlefield.
None of the Sarkaz raise their heads. They may already know of—or have grown accustomed to—the greater shadow that will soon envelop their kilometers-long procession.
Most of them move slowly as they cross the trenches left behind by the high-speed battleships.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I was just thinking... Look how long the line of soldiers is.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We've all traveled that road from Kazdel to Victoria before. We all know how long it is.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But if the Victorians break their word and open fire on the retreating Sarkaz forces, there'll be nothing you can do about it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Yes. That's how it's always been.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Maybe not immediately, but after the signal we send to all of Terra, every nation will be forced to respond.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Are you sure that will work?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Such a blatant retreat back to Kazdel will probably cause many countries to panic.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But there really is no better way.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Our squad must continue to present the strongest possible front to all factions. The moment we lose the strength to wield our weapons, we'll be devoured without a trace.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The same goes for the new 'King of Sarkaz'.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We must seize the initiative here.
The airship in the distance is faintly visible through the bones, and the ship's cannons remain locked in targeting mode.
A massive Catastrophe cloud still hovers around the ship, following the Sarkaz forces as they retreat.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But there's something else that's got me very worried.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Are you sure it's a good idea to have W guard Manfred?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: She's the best for the job.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: The squad has reached its destination.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: The weather is clear, and visibility is good.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Keep looking to the southeast.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: We've received the latest intelligence from the Ministry of Defense, which includes Kazdel's approximate coordinates.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Please closely monitor the Sarkaz army, to ensure their retreat home isn't a cover for another military maneuver.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Understood.
The officer does not, in fact, understand why he needs to monitor the Sarkaz.
However, out of respect for his comrades, he sits in the reconnaissance vehicle and stares intently at the data being sent back by the drones.
All is calm.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: There's nothing unusual to report at the moment, sir. By the way—and I'm just making small talk—Maylander rarely sends someone of your status to liaise with the military.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Heh, the Victorians think they've done a fine job covering up the disaster in Londinium.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Maylander needs to investigate the situation before we have a talk with them.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: ...Lieutenant! Lieutenant!

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: You are to report any new developments immediately!

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Of course, sir. There's nothing to report right now.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Nothing at all?!

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Wait. What's that...?
The officer puts down the communicator. The Catastrophe warning system on the vehicle is blaring an alarm.
He looks toward the capital district, but at this distance, he can barely make out the outline of the nomadic city.
But he can clearly see the massive shadow cast by the Catastrophe cloud, stretching from above the capital district all the way to where he stands.

steps.name: Respectful Attendant
steps.text: Yes. He knows you are familiar with the people of Siracusa, so he hopes you'll have a chance to display your talents this time.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Not to worry. The Sarkaz hordes are a chaotic, calamitous force, but they are ultimately mercenaries.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: We are now well aware that our neighbor, Victoria, has failed to keep them on a tight leash.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: But I shall not allow such filth to disrupt Leithanien's glorious Güldenesgesatz. Of this I am quite certain.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Please send this message along to your master—
The noble is interrupted by a suddenly darkening sky.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: ...What's going on?

steps.name: Respectful Attendant
steps.text: Come inside with me now, sir! It's a Catastrophe!

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Contact the base for further orders... Damn! We've got no signal! What the hell is going on? Push the fleet forward. Full throttle!

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Wait—
The data from the Catastrophe warning system sends a chill down his spine.
The cloud has stopped expanding, just as suddenly as it had appeared a few minutes ago.
The strong wind blows Originium dust up into the sky, but it doesn't fall back down.
Then the cloud starts to dissipate as the sunlight peaks through.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Can you hear me, lieutenant?

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: Yes, sir! The Catastrophe cloud appeared out of nowhere. There were no signs at all before it happened...

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Of course, of course. This was meant as a display, a show of force to intimidate us.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: You think the Sarkaz troops did this...?!

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: Maylander no longer requires your help with our investigation. Please withdraw at once. Of course, do not disclose any information about our cooperation.

steps.name: Columbian Military Officer
steps.text: ...Yes sir.

steps.name: Voice from the Communicator
steps.text: May Terra bless us.

steps.name: Kazimierzian Editor-in-Chief
steps.text: Enough. Deactivate the tip line. We have more than enough eyewitness accounts of the Catastrophe cloud!

steps.name: Kazimierzian Editor-in-Chief
steps.text: Everyone saw what happened. Those of us living in the high rises got an even closer look!

steps.name: Kazimierzian Editor-in-Chief
steps.text: For now, I need all of you to come up with explanations and file your stories. Everyone writes a report—whether you explain it away as an advertising hologram or new Arts from Leithanien, that's up to you.

steps.name: Kazimierzian Editor-in-Chief
steps.text: ...Do you need anything else?

steps.name: Kazimierzian Staff Member
steps.text: Sir, this call wasn't from a citizen...

steps.name: Kazimierzian Staff Member
steps.text: We just received word from our Messengers... Zwillingstürme, Laterano, Montelupe... Catastrophe clouds have appeared over the capitals of every nation.

steps.name: Kazimierzian Editor-in-Chief
steps.text: What about Deity Grypherburg and Max D.C.?

steps.name: Kazimierzian Staff Member
steps.text: ...Same situation.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: That little 'Amnannam' thingamajig is pretty handy. It can send a Catastrophe to someone's doorstep before you can blink.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Tch, no wonder Doctor and the hag were so nervous when we came to take it away, and the little bunny insisted on tagging along to keep an eye on me.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hmm...What if we just, like, destroyed every capital of the Core all at once?
While it may indeed be able to rain down disaster on those nations, that doesn't mean it can destroy them.
I have no doubt that doing so would bring nothing but retaliation against Kazdel. Our history has repeatedly proven this, even from the earliest records.
It would be unwise, Wiš'adel. In fact, you must use Amnannam sparingly—the strain it places on the mind and body is even greater than I imagined.
You just experienced that pain firsthand.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You don't get to tell me that, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Amnannam's potential extends far beyond intimidation, assuming we figure out the proper use for it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Their Highnesses had much higher hopes for it. Yes, it is a weapon, a deterrent, but more importantly, it is the means by which we will break free from our destiny—

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You know, you're even more annoying than Hoederer.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Don't forget who you are, dude. You're a prisoner, and we're only keeping you alive 'cause Kazdel needs you alive.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hell, the only reason we let the Military Commission stick around is that the surviving Sarkaz still need something to believe in on the way home.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Fucking Theresis sure thought of everything, huh?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...I'm guessing Hoederer saw this coming long ago too, didn't he?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This was always the Regent's overt strategy: to reunite a people—brought together once more by hatred—around Kazdel—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Even Babel and the Military Commission are working together again, united toward a common goal.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Yeah yeah, but don't expect to wriggle your way out of this one, Manfred. Remember what I said.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Wiš'adel...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: What, still got more to say?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If, someday, Kazdel really does normalize its relations with the other nations, just as Her Highness Theresa once strived for...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Then I, along with the rest of the Military Commission, will have to draw a clear line between ourselves and Kazdel.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: As the Sarkaz see it, outbloods bring only pain and hatred, just as we do to them.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Sooner or later, they will claim that we haven't paid for the crimes we have committed, and on that day I will be waiting for those hateful avengers to find us—

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Just shut up already. Stop acting like you're a saint or whatever.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Theresis and the rest of you assholes screwed up big time. You were so goddamned stupid I wish I could blow you to pieces right now.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Don't forget: almost all the lunatics who actually believed in your plan died in Londinium, along with the Nachzehrer.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You killed them with your own hands. There were hardly any left to even evacuate.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: But the Sarkaz will pay for their own mistakes.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Babel's not so spineless as to cast the entire Commission from the city just because a few dumbasses were bold enough to provoke Kazdel.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Her Highness would never do that, and neither will I.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: If they're stupid enough to come, I don't mind giving 'em a fight.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: But if you keep talking shit, I'll just toss you over to someone who's willing to put up with your crap.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: You're not afraid of it?

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Look at that moving Catastrophe cloud over there. It seems so far away, but I can't shake the feeling it might suddenly appear right above my head...

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: Of course I'm afraid. Who isn't afraid of Catastrophes?

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: But there's a trick I picked up in Sami: whenever I'm scared, I just pull my hat over my head, crouch down, and think of something happy. The things you're afraid of will disappear before you even know it.

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: After all, I'm just minding my own business—they wouldn't give me a hard time for no reason, would they?

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Just last week you said you'd lost count of how many times you'd been captured and interrogated by one of the Famiglie.

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: *sigh* I'm sorry for the trouble.

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: But misunderstandings always get cleared up in the end. I mean, you guys did let me go, didn't you?

spans.text: But misunderstandings always get cleared up in the end. I mean, you guys

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: ...I really can't figure out how you managed to make it all the way through Sami and Ursus in one piece. You ain't lying about that too, are ya?

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: I just happen to come across perfectly reasonable people like you all the time.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Hmph. Try reason your way out of Catastrophes, then.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Remind me again where you're going? Some place called 'Black Flow'?

steps.name: Mysterious Man
steps.text: Yes, and I'm also going home, friend, back home to Bolívar.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: That's one long-ass journey. An extra day or two won't make a difference. Besides, that tattered paper talisman you're carrying ain't gonna expire.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Anyhow, I advise you to wait for that parade of crazies to pass. They started a war; they can destroy cities.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Or maybe wait for someone or something else to test out the Catastrophe for you.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Just some friendly advice.

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Those devils are bold as hell—someone's bound to try and take a bite out of 'em sooner or later.
He can hear the terrifying roar of the Catastrophe cloud off in the distance, along with the faint rumble of battleship engines.
The Siracusan is right. It may be wiser not to get involved in this, however...

steps.name: Siracusan Mafioso
steps.text: Paryaqaqa, you ain't actually... fascinated by that cloud, are ya?

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: Maybe I am. I find it hard to hide my excitement whenever I encounter something I've never seen before.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: True, I paid a price for it back in Sami, but I just can't get rid of this bad habit.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: To be more precise, I want to take a look at the people walking beneath the Catastrophe cloud.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: How is it going? I hope no one is giving you any trouble.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Just another ordinary funeral.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: ...A funeral beneath a Catastrophe cloud is hardly ordinary. It's unfair to so many—they should have been able to return to Kazdel with us.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Death is the one form of equality most readily attainable to all, Misery.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The vast majority of the deceased have no relatives, nor even names.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: When I asked them to leave their final words, they could not even identify anyone who might remember them after they were gone.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I shrouded the burial site in mist to keep beasts away. Unfortunately, most of the dead were still unable to return to the furnace at home as they wished.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Logos, do you know what lies a little further up ahead?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: My previous missions... rarely required me to come this way.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Laterano is just south of here, not far.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: When Outcast and I went on missions together in this area, she'd often bring me here to drink.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: We once made a foolish bet—that I'd find a way to sneak in and try Lateran ice cream.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Well, I did it. No one caught me.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: But I never got the chance to tell her.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Ha. At least I'm not the one breaking my promise this time.

spans.text: not the one breaking my promise this time.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: So you deliberately refused the order to return to the ship with Ascalon.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You knew we'd pass through here during the retreat.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Don't try to guess my intentions, Logos.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: With Ascalon here, we'll have no issues escorting our fallen comrades and their tokens back to the ship.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Besides... she also needs some time to herself. To say goodbye to the past.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I tried speaking to her about the retreat, but she remained silent.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Perhaps she won't have anything to say about what happens next, either.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: She witnessed the end of an era, Logos. It couldn't have been easy for her, and I fear we'll have one less participant at our future meetings.
Misery lets out another sigh.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: No one can say for sure what will happen next.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: It's just like the Catastrophe cloud above our heads... I may not like this plan, but I must admit it's the best deterrent we have against those who wish to seize the chance to declare war on the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Without a strong measure like that to avoid war, there would only be more unnecessary sacrifices on the road back to Kazdel.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Violence is a means, never an end. There is nothing wrong with that.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Maybe I'm just a pessimist...

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: But I still think the rain will come down, sooner or later.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: Uh-huh. So can you let me go?

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Who the hell are you, anyway?

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: I'm really just an explorer.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: What kinda explorer could stop the lightning in a Catastrophe cloud? I-It's like the thunderbolts themselves are afraid of you...

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: Maybe they've taken a liking to me?

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: See? A few of them just landed right next to me!

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: You do realize that just makes you even more suspicious, right?

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Personally, I think the Catastrophe's sending a clear message—don't come near us, and don't try and test us!

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: Now now, let's not be hasty. I just wanted to study the strange Catastrophe cloud you created, as well as remind you that—

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: I don't like you.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: You tell too many lies.
The Sarkaz mercenary sizes up the man standing before him, and hesitates about whether to make a move.
This guy's the one you were talking about?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: He looks pretty normal to me.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You sure you got this right, old geezer?

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: He is giving off a particular scent, one I loathe.

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) 'Šmal'deqa'... 'enemies from outside'.

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: No... It is not coming from him, it is what he brought with him.

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: Strange. It seems to be... a piece of paper?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Pfft. You really are confused, you old coot.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: So does this mean we don't need to worry about him anymore? Hey! Why aren't you saying anything?

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Boss, I—

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I told you, call me 'Chairman' from now on. Tch, what a pain in the ass. Why did Hoederer have to make up all these stupid rules?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Only Her Highness should be called 'Chairman'...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Anyway, your squad's out here to scout, so just keep on scouting. Leave this guy to me.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You. If you've got something to say, say it. Don't try and pull a fast one on me.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I guarantee I'm faster than you.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: There's a fleet heading your way. Don't know which nation they're from—they've disabled all identifying signals.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: They're coming from that direction. The terrain provides a lot of cover. It would be easy to plan an ambush.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I guess everyone wants in on this.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Tch, what a bunch of cowards. Afraid of us, yet always acting cocky.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Alright, I'll pass on the word to the guys charging to their deaths on the frontlines

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: —Hello? Can you hear me? While you're out there, watch out for an ambush.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: So as a thank-you, how about I invite you to watch the Catastrophe cloud with me? You're here to 'explore', right?

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: Hahaha... I'd really rather not. I'm shaking in my boots here.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Alright. Your loss. Now scram. If any clueless Sarkaz grabs you again, just tell them who let you go—Wiš'adel.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: You have my thanks.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: That sure was a close call. If you hadn't rescued me, this journey would have been my last.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Drop the act around me. I know you got caught on purpose.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: It's so weird. Why do I keep running into people who have nothing to do with the Sarkaz, but want to help anyway?
The Liberi eyes the seemingly relaxed Sarkaz before him, quickly realizing she's likely the leader of the group—and that her attention has long since shifted away from him.
She is focused on the distant horizon. She is heeding his warning.
The wind brings with it the sounds of the land... or maybe the rumbling of ships' engines.
Conflicts, wars... the explorer has already seen too much along the way.

steps.name: Paryaqaqa
steps.text: *sigh*...

a.text: 'As always, we don't want to be the ones waiting for a beating.'
'All the Arts creations we sent out have been destroyed. They know we're getting closer, but I never planned on hiding anyway.'
'Some unlucky souls have to be sent to their deaths so the others can board the ship and fight. Will it be your squad or mine?'
'Follow the orders of Babel and the Military Commission—this isn't for you to decide on your own.'
'Kill every hostile you encounter. Anyone in the squad who spares an enemy or takes spoils from their comrades—kill them too.'
'Prepare the explosives. Set up altars along the route.'
'Normally, the altars' Arts can't penetrate the armor of high-speed battleships. But this time, we have the Catastrophe cloud on our side.'

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: They're here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: I knew going home wouldn't be that easy.
The earth is shaking.
The high-speed battleships slowly emerge from the shadows, blocking the Sarkaz's path forward.
The warrior launched a few charges like this while in Londinium, and considers himself one of the fortunate few.
He also knows full well that the path back to Kazdel is not a road, but a battlefield, full of corpses and awash in blood.
The Sarkaz procession stops at the edge of the firing range of the battleships' cannons.
The sky grows dark, as the black cloud overhead lets loose with rolling thunder. Their enemy is approaching.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Everyone, commence preparations like you were ordered.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Each of you just do your own job.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I don't want to catch any idiots of you showing off—

a.text: 'Halt.'
'You may not advance any further.'

steps.text: Only a few Sarkaz have noticed the young Cautus girl within their ranks.
She marches towards the head of the line.
Then, with a wave of her staff, the girl draws a line behind where she stands. The black line spreads across the earth.
A black wall rises up where the line once was.
An impregnable wall, woven of black silk threads, separates the two opposing forces.
The Sarkaz can no longer see the Cautus girl on the other side of the wall.
But one thing remains imprinted in their memories—the black crown floating above her head.
The King of Sarkaz.
Their king has not abandoned them? They have a new king?
But... why an outblood king?
The new king's voice resonates in the minds of every Sarkaz present. Meanwhile, the fleet sent to block them clearly hears her words:

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Sarkaz are going home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I will not rule out violence if necessary. I know full well the weight of this Black Crown.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa has already led the myriad souls away. For the first time, the Sarkaz have a choice.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I will not let her efforts be in vain.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Nor do I want the Sarkaz, or any of you, to start another war.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The cycle of hatred and revenge must end.
This is the first time Amiya has openly revealed her identity since Theresa taught her all there was to know about the Black Crown inside the Assimilated Universe.
Now she can hear noisy cries from amidst the Sarkaz.

a.text: 'Impossible! It can't be!'
'An outblood stole the Sarkaz's crown? How?! Why?!'
'She is our king? Do I have to make a tribute? What does she want from us?'
'Let's go! It's onto the next battlefield!'

steps.text: Terror, suspicion, reverence, ecstasy. A wave of emotions floods Amiya's mind.
In the past, she has made several attempts to explore the information stored within the Black Crown, but she has never gone this far.
The tide of information nearly overwhelms her. For millennia, the Sarkaz have desperately sought their 'King', chasing an elusive vision.
She tries her best to steady her thoughts and maintain the unshakable black wall.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I am no ruler, nor am I the King of Sarkaz.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the Sarkaz hate me for this, I will accept that.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I will show them the way forward, the path to end their suffering.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Both sides should stand down.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There won't be any more war.
The black wall still stands, just as the Catastrophe swirls above the wilderness.
After a long stalemate, the first battleship in the fleet begins to change direction.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Great. Finally...
The wave of thoughts suddenly fade away, and she hears an unusually clear voice—

a.text: '...Who are you?'

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Remain silent.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: As His Holiness commanded.

steps.name: Lateran Commando
steps.text: Even though the Sarkaz have committed countless crimes within our holy city? Even though Laterano has never before faced such provocation and desecration?

steps.name: Lateran Commando
steps.text: Even though their army is openly threatening the safety of our residents? Even then, we will not respond?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Yes. His Holiness believes that Laterano should not interfere in this matter.

steps.name: Lateran Commando
steps.text: I wish to see him. I'm going to file a protest!

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: ...We are unsure where he is right now.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The sudden disturbance of the halo, and the flood of information...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: For whatever reason, it suddenly became aware of something.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: 'A conversation'.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It is... having a conversation. With something similar to itself.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Since it has decided to make its choice, I am afraid I must follow suit. The new revelation it has showed us is something Laterano can no longer bear on its own.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Let me think... let's start with the first question.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: ...Who are you?

a.text: 'I have to admit, Your Holiness, that this is a long road.'
'Even without the whispers of the myriad souls trapped in Originium for millennia, it will still take a long time for the Sarkaz and this land to let go of their hatred.'
'Well then, Amiya, my child, what if we do not have that much time?'
'What if Terra is no longer in its infancy and has come to the point where it has to face its future—'
'Theresa warned me this might happen.'

steps.text: Someone walks into the static void.
He is following someone else's footsteps, although their footprints have vanished from this place forever.
The tower is still collapsing, a hint at everything that has transpired.
Although time has no meaning here, he must admit that he's a step late.
She is already completely out of reach.
Now all he can see is the golden ocean and the lonely diamond in the sky.

a.text: 'Amiya, not even I, the pope, know when or where the disaster will occur.'
'But I am certain that it will be a crisis that we've never faced before—'
'It is right before our eyes.'
